The simulation results show that the DC bus voltage based on double closed-loop structure with improved LADRC has better anti-disturbance performance when the grid voltage changes suddenly than the double closed-loop structure with LADRC.

articleTitle: Non-Fragile Control Design for Networked Systems
abstract: The problem of the non-fragile peak-to-peak control of quantitative state-feedback in networked systems is investigated in this paper, in which non-fragile controller is considered by the randomly occurring uncertainty. A new one-step design strategy will be implemented, while the controller and quantizer will be developed synchronously to ensure the peak-to-peak performance. Finally, the effectiveness of the design method is determined by utilizing an example of a 2DOF model of vehicle dynamics.

articleTitle: Dynamic Walking Locomotion Framework Based on Impulse Force Design and ZMP Principle
abstract: Walking gait has the strongest obstacle climbing ability for quadruped robot. The traditional static walking gait plans the ZMP trajectory only, which is low motion efficiency, slow speed and poor anti-disturbance performance. At present, force control is the core of balance locomotion method for quadruped robot, which can improve the adaptive ability of the robot to external forces and environmental disturbances during walking. However, the dynamic walking based on open-loop phase sequence can not guarantee the ZMP constrains all the time. Meanwhile, the center of mass needs to locate in the support area to ensure not falling in walking. In order to solve those problems, a dynamic walking framework combining ZMP phase sequence constraint and impulse feed-forward design is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a ZMP stability principle is introduced to gait phase planning. At the same time, the impulse force planning is used to control the inclination during swing. Combined with the ZMP trajectory planning, the robot motion efficiency has improved. Finally, through the experiments with simulation and physical platform, the proposed algorithm is test on stair climbing mission, and the results verify that the proposed framework has a stable dynamic walking performance.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-Based Arbitrary Convergence Time Congestion Control for TCP/AWM Network System
abstract: Aiming at the congestion control problem for TCP/AWM network system, an arbitrary convergence time congestion controller based on the disturbance observer is proposed in this paper. Firstly, in order to make the output signal track the expected queue within settling time, the free-will arbitrary time control (FATC) is used to design the equivalent controller. In addition, the super twisting control (STC) is introduced as the disturbance observer to solve the chattering problem caused by the traditional signum function, which results that the switching control is changed from discontinuous control to continuous control. Finally, all closed-loop signals are free-will arbitrary time stable. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Feature Fusion with Slim Non-Local Module for Multispectral Pedestrian Detection
abstract: Feature fusion plays a vital role in multispectral pedestrian detection system. Traditional fusion in different layers rely on simplely concat method for efficiency, but the pixel-wise spatial relationship in both short and long range are neglected. Towards this problem, non-local network provides a possible solution to cross-modality feature fusion, which is able to capture the long range relationship between pixels in the feature map from both RGB and thermal modalities. However, the naive utilization of non-local network brings significant memory footprint cost especially for the high resolution feature maps. To this end, we propose a slim non-local network, which compress the size of the attention map, leading to significant reduction of memory load. Besides, ablation studies with our slim non-local module for different stage are also investigated, which indicates that the optimal fusion schema comes from all the feature layers. Experimental results on KAIST dataset report that our method can outperform the baseline method with reasonable cost.

articleTitle: Agent Cluster Based on Adaptive Mechanism in Mosaic Warfare
abstract: The battlefield environment under the information warfare is complex and changeable. In order to solve the problem that communication is easily interfered and the combat interaction is not accurate enough in mosaic warfare, the adaptive mechanism is introduced into unmanned combatand and an adaptive cluster model based on "vision-perception-drive" is proposed. The agent with adaptive mechanism perceives the surrounding environment through vision, conducts internal autonomous simulation, and uses the principle of future state maximization(FSM) to decide its own movement direction. Experiments show that the adaptive mechanism can make the agents quickly form a team, and has good robustness. The characteristics of adaptive mechanism without interaction between agents have certain significance for the guidance and development of unmanned cluster cooperative warfare.

articleTitle: An asymmetric LKF robust load frequency control under random deception attacks
abstract: In this paper, H<inf>∞</inf> load-frequency controller for power system suffering from deception attacks is designed to keep the power system frequency stable. Firstly, the network-based load-frequency control(LFC) power system under the existence of deception attacks and load disturbance is established. Then, an asymmetric Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional(LKF) method is proposed to demonstrate the asymptotic stability of the LFC power system. Meanwhile, in terms of Lyapunov-Krasovskii stability theory, linear matrix inequalities and stochastic analysis technique, some sufficient conditions are expressed to guarantee the asymptotic stability of the LFC systems with the H<inf>∞</inf> performance index. Finally, numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Product Line Expansion for Quality Differentiated Manufacturers considering Product Sharing
abstract: In supply chain management, product line expansion is the core operation method of traditional manufacturers. In the sharing market, to eliminate the negative impact of product sharing, manufacturers expand the product line to attract consumers by providing rental products (lower quality than retail products). We study whether quality differentiated manufacturers will expand the product line. The results show that the low-quality manufacturer will expand the product line and whether the high-quality manufacturer expands the product line will be affected by quality differentiation. When the quality difference between retail products and the quality difference between retail products and rental products are low, the high-quality manufacturer expands the product line; otherwise, it does not expand the product line. Furthermore, compared to manufacturers not expanding the product line, the equilibrium leads to a Pareto improvement. When both manufacturers expand the product line, they will gain more profits. When only the low-quality manufacturer expands its product line, the low-quality manufacturer gains more profit and the high-quality manufacturer’s profit remain unchanged.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of two-dimensional parabolic equations with general terms
abstract: In this paper, the stability of classical explicite scheme, classical implicit scheme and Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for two-dimensional parabolic equations with general terms is studied. The Fourier method is used to analyze the three schemes. Finally, the stability conditions of the three schemes are obtained through theoretical analysis. Numerical experiments verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Adaptive output tracking for a hybrid wave-ODE system subject to unknown sinusoidal disturbance
abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the output tracking problem for a hybrid wave-ODE system coupling an elastic string with a rigid body at one end. The control force acts on the rigid body and the output is at the other end where is subject to an unknown sinusoidal disturbance. By constituting auxiliary system and internal model dynamic, an adaptive method is developed to identify the unknown frequency of disturbance. An error-based adaptive dynamic compensator is proposed to achieve exponential output tracking. The well-posedness and stability of the closed-loop system are proved by employing the semigroup theory. The numerical simulations are presented to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A hierarchical anti-swing control method based on end effector for 2D underactuated overhead cranes system
abstract: In this paper, a hierarchical anti-swing control scheme based on end effector is proposed for a two-dimensional overhead crane. The proposed control scheme consists of a passivity-based controller and a sliding mode controller. The passivity-based controller is used to suppress load swing and track virtual position, which will deduce desired crane acceleration. The sliding mode controller is used to control crane acceleration. The stability of the proposed closed-loop system is verified by using Lyapunov function and the LaSalle’s invariance theorem. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is shown by simulation results. Specifically, the proposed controller guarantees accurate control of crane position and swift suppression of load swing.

articleTitle: A Vehicle Target Detection Method Based on Feature Level Fusion of Infrared and Visible Light Image
abstract: Single-mode recognition method remains a difficulty problem in target detection and recognition of road vehicle targets in complex urban situations. Hence, using the advantages of obtaining different feature information from infrared and visible images in different situations is considered. We propose a feature level infrared and visible image fusion target detection method based on deep learning. This method first obtains the registered infrared visible image, extracts the image features respectively through two main feature extraction networks, passes through the feature fusion layer, passes into the feature pyramid network to obtain the effective feature layer, and then carries out classification prediction and regression prediction. On the test set, the mAP of the fusion method is 0.89, which is higher than that using only visible images (the mAP is 0.82) and only infrared images (the mAP is 0.79) on the same test set. At the same time, in the night environment, the mAP of the fusion method is much higher than other deep learning frameworks. The experimental results show that the infrared and visible image fusion target detection method realized in this paper has certain advantages over the traditional methods and has a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Potential Function-based Satellite Attitude Control for Moving Target Tracking with Input Saturation Constraint and Time-Varying Inertia
abstract: The problem of image-based satellite attitude tracking control for moving target is studied when input saturation constraint and time-varying inertia exist during the maneuver. The potential function is designed to handle the image-based attitude constraint for moving target tracking. Then an adaptive backstepping controller is designed for attitude tracking control in the presence of uncertain time-varying inertia, and the auxiliary system is employed to ensure the satisfaction of input saturation constraint. The stability analysis shows that the proposed control law guarantees the asymptotical convergence of the tracking errors. Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the efficacy and performance of the presented controller under input saturation constraint and time-varying inertia.

articleTitle: Simulation Research of Binocular Machine Vision System
abstract: This paper proposes a binocular vision system. It adopts humanoid design, has four degrees of freedom, and realizes complete synchronization in the horizontal direction at the same time, expounding the application of binocular stereo vision principle and control theory in visual synchronization. The control system uses voltage as an input signal to control the angular velocity of two identical motors in a parallel circuit. Establish the transfer function model of the motor and the four-degree-of-freedom parallel human-like binocular vision mechanism system respectively, and then use SIMULINK to simulate, evaluate the simulation results, analyze the parameters of the curve, and give the optimization path to optimize the response curve.

articleTitle: Soft-sensing Prediction of Mining SAG Mill Load
abstract: Taking the semi-autogenous mill, a commonly used equipment in the grinding process, as the research object, the problem of continuous and stable operation of the production process in the best working conditions is discussed to improve the utilization rate of resource and achieve the purpose of coordinating energy saving and production capacity. The main reason why the semi-autogenous mill cannot achieve economical operation is that its load is difficult to realize on-line detection. In order to ensure the continuous operation of grinding production and prevent the occurrence of empty grinding and full grinding, the staff can only conservatively feed the mine through experience, resulting in unbalanced operating efficiency. The proposed PSPCAW-SVM composite soft-sensing algorithm is selected, and the soft-sensing model of the semi-autogenous mill load is established according to the sample data of the process, which is used for the online monitoring of the mill load, and the accuracy and stability of model is evaluated through the calculation of simulation prediction results and performance indicators.

articleTitle: Research on a panoramic video transmission scheme based on multi-view switching within the human eye's field of view
abstract: In today's Internet era, people have increasingly higher requirements for video clarity and breadth of vision. The scene information that can be expressed by traditional video is limited, and it is difficult to meet people's needs anymore, and panoramic video has emerged as the times require. Panoramic video can bring people an immersive and interactive audio-visual experience. However, due to its own characteristics, panoramic video with ultra-high resolution and ultra-high bit rate has a high demand for network bandwidth during network transmission. This paper compares the existing panoramic video transmission schemes, analyzes the advantages and disadvantages of each scheme, and proposes a transmission scheme based on multi-view switching within the human eye’s field of view, and then verifies the effectiveness of the scheme in saving network bandwidth by building a live platform.

articleTitle: Optimal Control of Discrete-time Linear Switched Systems with Dynamical Logic-based Switching
abstract: This paper investigates the finite-horizon quadratic optimal control problem of discrete-time switched systems with dynamical logic-based switching, where the switching signal is generated by a dynamical logic decision layer. By using the semi-tensor product of matrices and the vector representation of logic, the logic-state and the continuous-state are merged to a single state vector and the original switched system is transferred into an equivalent ordinary switched system. By using the principle of dynamic programming, both the logic control input for the decision layer and the control for the continuous-state layer are designed to minimize the quadratic cost function. An example is provided to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Finite-time consensus control for multi-agent systems with channel fading via sliding mode technique
abstract: This article concentrates on the finite-time leader-following consensus tracking problem for second-order multi-agent systems (MASs). Due to the effect of time delay, amplitude attenuation and random noise/interference, the transmission among followers may be inevitably suffered the channel fading. Based on the fading data received from neighbor agents, the consensus tracking error variables are designed firstly. Then, a consensus control scheme is proposed via sliding mode control (SMC) and Lyapunov stability theory, the consensus controller is designed to force the states of MASs to achieve the terminal sliding surface in finite time and maintain on it, and the consensus of MASs can be ensured in finite time. Finally, a numerical example is demonstrated for showing the effectiveness and applicability of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Design and development of AGV intelligent feeding control system for carbon calcination
abstract: in the production process of carbon enterprises, the metallurgical raw materials added to the calciner are mainly carried out on-site through manual operation equipment. There are low feeding efficiency and low degree of automation. There are high temperature, dust and potential safety hazards in on-site manual operation; Based on the upgrading of the feeding control system of a calciner, this paper develops an intelligent feeding control system integrating wireless control technology, coded displacement sensor, radar obstacle avoidance, weighing and metering, programmable controller and other modern control technologies. The system realizes the automatic navigation and accurate positioning of the feeding vehicle through segmented braking and parking algorithm and speed adaptive algorithm, Automatic feeding realizes the purpose of Safe Obstacle Avoidance and unattended.

articleTitle: Accurate Active and Unbalanced Harmonic Power Sharing of Islanded Microgrid Based on Small-AC-Signal Injection
abstract: The structure of islanded microgrids is complex and has many problems. For this problem of equalizing the fundamental active power, many articles use the traditional droop control, which cannot simulate the physical characteristics of inertia and damping in the power generation process, which are considered by the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology. The mismatch of the feeder impedance can lead to the inequality of unbalanced harmonic power for the parallel inverters. To address this problem, a control method is proposed that injects an additional small AC signal (SACS)into the output voltage of each inverter and adds an adaptive virtual impedance. This method is similar to the conventional active-frequency droop control, where the output frequency of the injected SACS is linearly related to the output unbalanced harmonic power. When the unbalanced harmonic power rises, the output frequency of the injected signal also rises. And the virtual impedance on the negative sequence series is adjusted by detecting the active power generated by the injected SACS. When the system is stable, the frequency of the injected SACS in each inverter will be the same, and the sum of the virtual inductance and the feeder inductance of each inverter will be the same. The active power and the unbalanced harmonic power of the parallel distributed generator set can be equally shared without communication.

articleTitle: A simplified fractional-order fuzzy logic controller with dynamic parameters for an unmanned underwater vehicle
abstract: The performance of a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) largely depends on its inference rules and control inputs. In this paper, fractional calculus is introduced into the fuzzy control inference rules. It can accumulate overall information within a certain range of a function, which is helpful for the system to resist external disturbances. Firstly, a control scheme of a simplified fractional-order fuzzy logic controller (FD-SIFLC) with dynamic parameters is proposed for the controller design of an unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV). The presented control method employs a single-input FLC with fractional calculus, and the scale factor changes with the relative error magnitude. The controlled system maintains the accuracy of its depth control while enabling other variables to exhibit better transient and steady-state performance. By using Matlab/Simulink<sup>®</sup> to conduct simulation experiments, the control performance of FD-SIFLC and SIFLC for the depth control of UUV is compared. During the simulation, the controlled system is disturbed by ocean waves. The simulation results show that, compared with SIFLC, FD-SIFLC can make the response curve of each variable smoother. Moreover, the proposed control method can improve the working efficiency and service life of an UUV control system.

Author Keywords: Dynamic Parameters and Unmanned Underwater Vehicle

articleTitle: New Framework for Highlights Removal Based on CycleGAN
abstract: Highlights detection and removal is hot topic in computer vision. It exists in high-gloss leather, glass, plastic, metal parts, and other mirror-reflective objects. Deep convolutional neural network-based highlight removal techniques can learn material rendering parameters supervised by a large number of paired datasets to automatically remove highlights from object surfaces. However, in reality, the datasets are usually unpaired. It is difficult to obtain a large number of paired images. To deal with the unpaired data, dual learning (CycleGAN) can make full use of unlabeled data. Therefore, based on S2D-NET, a new framework is proposed to address the above problem. The main contribution is that: a confidence map with independent averages is proposed to guide the network to quickly search for the initial value, which can solve the problem of slow network convergence due to the lack of a very strict mathematical definition to distinguish specular reflection components from diffuse reflection components. The experiments are compared with the latest three methods. It is found that the SSIM and PSNR values of our proposed algorithm are improved.

articleTitle: Improved gravitational search and identification of multivariable Hammerstein systems
abstract: The multivariable Hammerstein system has been widely used in various complex industrial systems. Therefore, it is very important to identify the parameters of this type of systems. Due to the complexity and diversity of the nonlinear part in the multivariable Hammerstein system, the difficulty of system identification increases. The improved chaotic gravitational search algorithm (ICGSA) is used to estimate the parameters of the static nonlinear part, the linear part and the colored noise part in the multivariable Hammerstein systems. The simulation results show that the ICGSA can effectively identify the multivariable Hammerstein systems. In addition, the ICGSA is proved to be superior to the chaotic gravitational search algorithm (CGSA) and the forgetting factor stochastic gradient algorithm (FFSG) in identification accuracy by comparing with CGSA and FFSG.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling and Application of Anti-Submarine Decision-Aided System Based on Neural Network
abstract: With the development of aviation anti-submarine technology, there are many advanced anti-submarine aircraft equipped with decision-aided system. Aiming at the problem of how to apply anti-submarine decision-aided system, this paper studies an effectiveness evaluation model based on neural network by taking the parallel sector pattern as an example. Simulation results show that the trained model is extremely accurate, which can guide pilots to set more precise parameters of anti-submarine decision-aided system in real time without long time Monte-Carlo simulation. In practice, this model can provide a theoretical reference for the anti-submarine warfare.

articleTitle: Design of Einstein Chess algorithm based on CNN and UCT algorithm
abstract: For Einstein Chess pruning operation, a UCT algorithm fused with convolutional neural network is proposed by us, which is divided into two main parts. In the first part, to obtain the dynamic valuation function - UCT algorithm, the dynamic valuation function is integrated into the UCT algorithm. This algorithm adds a probability layer to the UCT algorithm based on the "attack value" and "threat value" of the two players, and can adjust the valuation method based on the state of the position. But the valuation of this algorithm is proportional to depth, which increases the time consumption. As a result, the dynamic valuation function-UCT algorithm line data is used as a training data set and trained with a neural network to produce a model with an error of around 2%. In the second part, the training model is introduced into the Einstein Chess line process in two stages: the trained neural network model is initially used for pruning, and then the UCT algorithm is used for decision making. To test the algorithm's viability, the upgraded neural net-UCT algorithm is played against the dynamic valuation function-UCT algorithm, and experimental results show that the neural net-UCT algorithm has a 63. 37% win rate.

articleTitle: Distributed Conditional Gradient Algorithm for Two-Network Saddle-point Problem
abstract: We consider a two-network saddle-point problem with constraints, whose projections are expensive. We propose a projection-free algorithm, which is referred to as Distributed Frank-Wolfe Saddle-Point algorithm (DFWSP), which combines the gradient tracking technique and Frank-Wolfe technique. We prove that the algorithm achieves O(1/k<sup>2</sup>) convergence rate for strongly-convex-strongly-concave saddle-point problems. We empirically shows that the proposed algorithm has better numerical performance than the distributed projected saddle-point algorithm.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Second Order Sliding Mode Control for Vehicle Platoon Subjected to Uncertainties and External Disturbances
abstract: In real-life vehicle platoon systems, vehicle aerodynamics parameters and unknown disturbance are usually hard to measure or estimate accurately, which may reduce the safety and comfort of the platoon system. To this end, an extended state observer (ESO) based on super twisting algorithm (STA) is proposed to estimate the lumped disturbance accurately in finite time. On this basis, a continuous super twisting controller (STC) is designed to ensure the string stability of the platoon system. Compared with the traditional sliding mode control (SMC) method, the predominant control performance of the STC guarantees faster convergence rate and smaller transient response of the closed-loop interconnected vehicular systems. In addition, the continuous control signal can alleviate the chattering caused by the discontinuous switching item, which can improve the driving comfort of the vehicle platoon. Finally, simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed observer and control method.

articleTitle: Event-Triggered MPC for Disturbed Nonlinear Systems via A Differential-Integral Mechanism
abstract: In this paper, the event-triggered model predictive control (ET-MPC) problem for the disturbed nonlinear system is studied, and a novel event-triggered mechanism (ETM) on the basis of a differential-integral (DI) type method is designed. Different from the existing triggering mechanism, we construct the ETM by combining the differential and integral of the error between the optimal prediction state and the actual one in the same prediction time period. Then, under the dual-mode control strategy, the DI type ET-MPC algorithm is established, and sufficient conditions are obtained to ensure the feasibility and stability of the algorithm. Finally, the simulation comparison verifies the effectiveness and the advantages of the developed algorithm.

articleTitle: Spectrum Analysis of PWM Waveform with DC Bus Voltage Ripple Based on Cascaded H-Bridge Converters
abstract: The cascaded H-bridge converter is a promising approach for high voltage and high power applications. A group of series-connected submodules with independent DC power supplies can be used to obtain excellent output voltage performance through low switching frequency. However, the DC bus voltage ripple will cause additional harmonics to the output voltage, which will cause output voltage distortion and reduce the output performance of the converter. This paper theoretically analyzes the harmonic voltage of the pulse width modulation converter with the DC bus voltage ripple, and gives the expression of the output voltage applied by a double Fourier series. This analysis reveals how the modulation signal and DC power supply interact with the carrier signal to produce undesired harmonics in the PWM signal, which provides a theoretical basis for undesired harmonic suppression. The theoretical results from the analysis are validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault-tolerant Control for Aerocraft with Actuator Failure and Perturbation
abstract: An adaptive fault-tolerant controller is designed based on the mathematical model of UAV with actuator failure and random disturbance. The controller is composed of a series of adaptive laws. Through online estimation of fault factors and disturbance factors, it compensates the influence of actuator faults and random disturbances on the system, and realizes the fault-tolerant control of the UAV system. Using active fault-tolerant control technology, an adaptive control gain equation is designed to make the obtained closed-loop system gradually stable without knowing the actuator fault and disturbance boundary information. The Matlab simulation experiment verifies the effectiveness of this adaptive fault-tolerant control method.

articleTitle: Adaptive tracking control for stochastic nonlinear systems with unknown virtual control coefficients
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive tracking controller for stochastic nonlinear systems with unknown virtual control coefficients (UVCCs). Without using the Nussbaum gain technique (NGT), the controller is designed by employing an inequality, which requires much less complex computations. Novel adaptive controllers are constructed to compensate parameter uncertainties and UVCCs. To validate the effectiveness and superiority of the presented control method, a numerical simulation example and a practical example are given in the end of the paper.

articleTitle: A Novel PSO Approach for Cooperative Task Assignment of Multi-UAV Attacking Moving Targets
abstract: Collaborative task assignment is the fundamental research of multi-UAV coordinated control problem. The key factors affecting the task assignment are analyzed and a comprehensive evaluation system is established considering the range, time window and attack reward. In the light of it, an optimal particle swarm (PSO) task assignment algorithm is proposed based on local random search (LRS) and variable neighborhood search (VNS), and a particle swarm codec algorithm is designed to solve the "deadlock" problem caused by simultaneous attacks. Meanwhile, the adaptive learning factors are introduced during the process of particles updating. To improve the global search capability of the algorithm, the LRS algorithm is embedded in the framework of VNS-PSO. Finally, some simulation experiments are proposed to verify the effectiveness of optimized PSO. Compared with VNS-PSO, LRS-VNS-PSO has better global searching ability to solve the task allocation problem in the scenario of simultaneous attack of multiple UAVs.

articleTitle: A Servo Simulation Test Calibration and Compensation Method for Hardware-in-the-loop Simulation of Aerocraft Control System
abstract: Aiming at the system errors caused by the original servo simulation test environment and the method errors caused by the calculation methods of transient, position and frequency characteristics in the semi-physical simulation test of the aircraft control system; a semi-physical servo simulation test system for the control system was designed and implemented. The servo simulation test system is mainly composed of a servo mechanism, an analog load table, a swing angle displacement sensor, a data acquisition board, a swing angle displacement acquisition computer, and a connecting cable. Through the unified test process and test method, as well as environmental calibration and test compensation, the dynamic and static test of the open loop servo mechanism is realized. The test results show that the method can detect various technical indicators of the servo mechanism, quickly assessing whether the servo mechanism meets the requirements of the simulation test with good real-time performance.

articleTitle: A Decomposition-based Constrained Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm with An Infeasibility Utilization Mechanism for UAV Path Planning
abstract: Evolutionary algorithm has been used to solve unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning problems. Usually, a UAV path planning problem is modelled as a constrained optimization problem, and the goal for evolutionary algorithms is to find a collision-free trajectory with respect to the constraints, which requires the algorithms equipping not only a powerful search engine but an effective constraint-handling technique. In the community of constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, an essential idea is how to make good use of the informative infeasible solutions during the evolution process, which can significantly improve performance of the algorithms. To the best of our knowledge, this has seldom been explored in UAV path planning problems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a decomposition-based constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm with an infeasibility utilization mechanism for solving UAV path planning problem. UAV path planning represented by the B-Spline curve is first formulated as a bi-objective optimization problem, i.e., minimizing the travelling distance and the risk of a UAV, with three constraints including the minimum flight height, the maximum flight height and minimum flight angle. Then a decomposition-based constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithm that can utilize the information containing in infeasible solutions is adopted to solve the constrained optimization problem. To further make good use of the infeasible solutions found by the algorithm, an infeasible utilization mechanism is proposed to guide the search to the optimal regions. The experimental results have indicated that the proposed algorithm is superior over the compared algorithm in terms of finding a set of well-distributed and well-converged non-dominated solutions.

articleTitle: Design of Missile Roll Autopilot based on Linear Extended State Observer
abstract: With the expansion of missile envelope and the improvement of missile combat effect in recent years, the control of missile roll channel is faced with many kinds of unknown disturbances, such as oblique-blowing moment, additional torque at high angle-of-attack, periodic interference of spin tail, severe noise and so on, which are very difficult to be modeled or analyzed accurately. The traditional PID roll autopilot cannot keep the command tracking effectively under these disturbances. Based on the ADRC idea, this paper designs a kind of LESO observer for missile roll channel without changing the original control parameters or structure, which can effectively estimate the disturbance and realize stable tracking of the roll angle command under all kinds of disturbance conditions.

articleTitle: Bearing fault diagnosis based on multiscale dilated convolutional neural network
abstract: In recent years, the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings has become a significant research direction. This paper proposes a new intelligent diagnosis method for the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. In this paper, a 2D-MDCNN model structure is proposed. Firstly, the 2D grayscale map of the original vibration signal and the wavelet transform spectrogram are fused, and the fused 2D hybrid feature image is imported into the model using the multiscale and dilation convolution. It has two advantages: 1) the wavelet transform and 2D gray map can combine the signal’s time domain and frequency domain, while the 2D gray map can fully ensure the information extraction. 2) Using multiscale and dilation convolution, the information can be extracted at different scales, significantly improving the feature extraction capability and expanding the perceptual field by dilation convolution.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Force Tracking Using Nonlinear Observer
abstract: This paper focuses on the development of a control scheme capable of tracking contact forces explicitly. Specifically, the nonlinear observer, admittance control and adaptive sliding mode control are integrated into a single framework. When the force sensor is absent, a nonlinear observer, which serves as a reaction force observer, can be used to estimate the contact force. Furthermore, in order to track the force profile explicitly, admittance control is introduced to transform the desired contact force into the desired position signal. An adaptive sliding mode controller is designed to track the desired position and meanwhile compensate the estimation errors of contact forces caused by nonlinear observer. The stability of the whole system under the proposed controller can be guaranteed by the Lyapunov function. Finally, several simulations are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Solving the Pose of Bio 3D Printing based on Neural Network
abstract: Obtaining the pose state information of the printing nozzle in real time and performing error compensation is an important means to improve the accuracy of biological 3D printing. Traditional pose solving methods such as Newton iteration method and Analysis method have problems such as difficulty in selecting the initial value and slow calculation speed. To solve the above problems, a biological 3D printing pose solution algorithm based on the Elman neural network optimized by genetic algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the kinematics model of the biological 3D printing platform is established, then the GA-Elman neural network is established and the inverse solution of the platform is used as a training sample, and the pose information is solved by the method of network learning, and finally the accuracy of the algorithm is verified by simulation. The simulation results show that the algorithm has high calculation accuracy and fast solution speed, and can quickly and accurately solve the pose of biological 3D printing.

articleTitle: Research on the Taxiing Control Method of a Small Full-Wing UAV under the Sensor Constraints
abstract: In order to solve the problem that the yaw angle measured by the small full-wing UAV during the taxiing process is susceptible and the course angle is unreliable at low speeds, a control approach which uses both yaw angle and course angle to control the taxiing process is proposed.Firstly, a dynamic model of the full-wing UAV during taxiing is established. Secondly, by improving the vector field trajectory tracking method, a linear trajectory tracking method is designed. Finally, based on the active disturbance rejection control method(ADRC), a taxiing direction controller is designed which uses the corrected course angle as the controlled state. Simulation and experimental results show that the designed controller has a good control performance, and can control the full-wing UAV taxiing along the correct trajectory under the condition of inaccurate yaw angle measurement.

articleTitle: Numerical forecast of the operating performance of underwater robots in autonomous navigation mode
abstract: In this paper, the scheme design and sampling mechanism of observation-level ROV are completed, and the operational performance of underwater robots in autonomous navigation mode is predicted numerically. According to the sliding mesh theory, the numerical simulation of the self-walking performance of the ROV body multi-propeller coupling system is completed. Based on the method of transmitting multi-computational domain flow field data from the sliding mesh, the dynamic problems such as the full body and multi-propeller fully coupled motion in the direct flight and the lower submersion are calculated numerically, and the manipulation performance of the observation stage ROV in autonomous navigation mode is predicted numerically. The results show that its navigation and observation functions meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: An End-to-End Lane-Keeping Approach Using Light Weighted Neural Network
abstract: We proposed a light weighted neural network to perform lane-keeping task in simple scenarios by predicting steering commands directly from the image input. In order to make it run on low-performance embedded devices, we used a HLS based binary threshold segmentation method to assist feature extraction, and the neural network behind has only four convolutional layers and two fully connected layers. The experimental results show that this model can extract the lane features and determine current steering commands synthetically. Deployed on a small car with a RK3399 development board and a front-view camera, this model achieved an inference speed at 10 fps, and can automatically keep the car in the lane without manual intervention.

articleTitle: Multimodal Perception based Autonomous Exploration with Active Camera Control in Unknown Environments
abstract: Autonomous exploration in the unknown environment is a fundamental problem of robot autonomy, however, it is always difficult to improve the efficiency of a robot to reconstruct its surroundings. In this paper, based on multimodal sensory fusion and active camera control, we proposed an active exploration algorithm that allows a robot highly efficiently reconstruct a complete map. First, we present a multimodal perception based map fusion algorithm to integrate 3D spatial information into 2D maps for better computational performance. Then, an active camera control algorithm is designed to take full advantage of the camera’s mobility during exploration so that the robot can reduce the cost of exploration time and path length. Moreover, we establish an active exploration framework, which further leads to a significant improvement in map coverage and reconstruction efficiency. Compared with the traditional exploration algorithm and the passive fixed camera platform, simulation results show that the map coverage and the exploration efficiency are improved by 10-20% and 33% respectively, which demonstrates the advantages of our method.

articleTitle: Application of humanoid intelligent control system in cement clinker calcination process
abstract: Clinker calcination is the core part of cement production process, which is characterized by multivariable, strong coupling, large hysteresis and complex and variable working conditions. It is difficult to establish an accurate mathematical model for this process, and it is difficult to achieve satisfactory control results by using conventional single control methods. Therefore, this paper designs a humanoid intelligent control system containing two control levels: conventional control and humanoid intelligent control, and conducts control research on the key kiln link in the clinker calcination process. First, according to the data characteristics of different controlled objects, LOWESS and sliding average filtering methods are selected for smoothing. Then, the steady state judgment of each process link is performed, and different control strategies are selected according to their operating status. Finally, the control system is applied in an actual cement clinker production line. The operation results show that the humanoid intelligent control system proposed in this paper not only realizes the automatic control of clinker calcination process, but also controls the key process parameters stably within a certain range, and its fluctuation is significantly lower than that of manual control. It not only saves the investment of human resources, but also makes the operation state more stable, which lays the foundation for the next optimization of cement production and has good application prospects.

articleTitle: Automatic Train Operation for Heavy-Haul Trains Based on Adaptive Nonsingular Terminal Sliding Mode Control
abstract: This study proposes a novel automatic train operation approach for heavy haul trains. The goal is to design a train trajectory tracking approach by simultaneously taking in-train coupler forces, non-negligible control command response processes, and parameter uncertainty into consideration. A three-order multiple-point-mass train model with consideration of command response process is established. Then by dividing the whole train into locomotive and wagon groups, the controller based on adaptive nonsingular terminal sliding mode control approach is designed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated in a real-world case study.

Author Keywords: adaptive nonsingular terminal sliding mode control

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Planning Based on A* Algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the problems of robot path planning in complex environment, an improved A* algorithm is proposed to search the shortest path of robots. Firstly, PRM algorithm is utilized to construct probability map. Secondly, the constructed probability map is used to replace the nodes in the conventional A* algorithm. Then, A* algorithm is applied to search the shortest path in the probability map. Finally, a host of experiments verity the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Response Control Method of PMSM in Field Weakening Region for Electric Vehicle
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the load torque of an electric vehicle changes with the road conditions during the high-speed driving process, the vehicle's maneuverability is deteriorated, and a vehicle permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) field weakening region high dynamic response control method is proposed.. First, through theoretical analysis, a mathematical model of the high-speed optimal working area of the vehicle PMSM is established, and the factors that affect the dynamic response of the vehicle PMSM in the traditional method are pointed out. Then, for this factor, a method of removing the torque PI adjustment and optimizing the field weakening algorithm is proposed. New control method. Finally, Simulink simulation and experiment prove that the control method proposed in this paper has faster response ability compared with the traditional control strategy.

articleTitle: Multi School Bus Routing Problem with Road Safety Factor via A Heuristic Algorithm
abstract: In this paper, a heuristic algorithm is used to consider the multi-school bus route planning problem with road safety factor. According to the requirements of school bus route planning, constraints such as school bus capacity, station capacity, and maximum operating time are considered, and the safety factor of the road is integrated. Finally, the safest and optimal path scheme is obtained through the corresponding algorithm. This paper proposes the construction method of road safety index, applies it to specific cases, and proposes a corresponding heuristic algorithm in order to solve the problem. Finally, numerical examples are used to illustrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved SMOTE based LSDA for Class Imbalanced Fault Diagnosis in TE Industrial Process
abstract: With the technological progress, industrial processes are developing towards intelligence, and the different classes of data collected show imbalanced features due to the new technologies put into the production process. Due to the imbalance of data classes, it brings difficulties to fault diagnosis. To address the imbalance, high-dimensional and non-linear characteristics of data in the actual production process, this paper proposes a novel fault diagnosis method with improved SMOTE-LSDA (ISMOTE-LSDA). Firstly, in ISMOTE-LSDA, an improved synthetic minority over-sampling technique (ISMOTE) algorithm is used to resample the imbalanced samples and expand the few classes of fault samples. The ISMOTE uses not only the Euclidean distance but also the cosine distance to calculate the K nearest neighbors (KNN) distance, and the nearest neighbor effect is more accurate. Then the manifold learning locality sensitive discriminant analysis (LSDA) algorithm is used to dimensionality reduction of high and non-linear balance samples to extract meaningful data features. Finally, an integrated learning Adaboost classifier is used for fault classification. The TE chemistry process is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed ISMOTE-LSDA method. The experimental simulation results show that the proposed method has better fault diagnosis accuracy compared to the traditional feature extraction methods which is suitable for the fault diagnosis process with unbalanced data classes.

articleTitle: Trajectory Design and Guidance Method of Multi-constraint Reentry and Glide section Based on H-V Planning and Gaussian Pseudo-Spectral Method
abstract: This paper presents an improved trajectory design and guidance method for long-range anti-aircraft missile re-entry glide segment based on H-V profile. The H-V trajectory of the glide segment is designed as cosine function, and the feasible domain of its key parameters is verified by simulation, which can avoid the problem of singularity of the roll Angle, so that no feasibility analysis and correction are required. By combining the Gauss pseudo-spectral trajectory optimization with H-V trajectory design, a feasible trajectory satisfying the re-entry corridor constraint can be quickly generated.

articleTitle: The Convex-Relaxation-Based Method for Power Flow Analysis
abstract: Power flow analysis is the most fundamental problem in the power system, which guides energy’s operation, dispatch, and control. This paper proposes a novel method for power flow calculation with the convex-relaxation technique. An unrelated variable can be represented with the linear constraints by setting the four sets of voltage variables with three stages of the newly-defined variables. The second-order cone relaxation replaces the non-linearity in the power flow relationship. Thus, the power flow calculation becomes a convex optimization problem. Both of the solving efficiency and uniqueness of the solution can be guaranteed at the same time because of the advantages of convex optimization. The availability of the proposed method is tested by the IEEE benchmark system.

articleTitle: Constrained Neural Adaptive Control for Scramjet-Powered Hypersonic Space Vehicle
abstract: A neural adaptive control for hypersonic space vehicle (HSV) with angle of attack (AOA) constraint is investigated. The control system is decomposed into velocity subsystem and altitude subsystem. For velocity subsystem, a neural adaptive controller is proposed to handle the saturation problem of the scramjet input (i.e., fuel-to-air equivalency ratio, FER). Aiming at the AOA constraint problem of the altitude subsystem, a neural adaptive controller based on barrier Lyapunov function is designed for altitude tracking. Simulation shows that the proposed control has fast tracking performance and can synthetically deal with constrained AOA, model uncertainty and external disturbances.

articleTitle: Dynamic Shapley value for dynamic network games with perishable goods
abstract: This paper investigates a two-stage network game in which each stage exists given a minimum spanning tree game containing perishable goods. By the defined cooperative behavior, the players act at each stage to construct the cost matrix of the network and obtain the corresponding minimum spanning tree based on the obtained network. At the end of the first stage of the game, a particular player is affected due to the actions of all players and thus leaves the game in the second stage with a certain probability. The total cost of the whole game is considered to be equal to the sum of the costs of the two stages. After defining the characteristic functions of the game, dynamic Shapley values are constructed and their time-consistency is investigated.

articleTitle: Fault Detection For Dynamic System Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
abstract: To solve the problem of multivariable time series fault detection, a Long Short Term Memory Generative Adversarial network (LSTM-GAN) model was proposed in this paper. The contributions are as follows: 1. generators and discriminators were constructed from LSTM Network to capture the dynamic times series related characteristics; 2. then Generative Adversarial Network was introduced to generate pseudo-samples from a latent space to capture the real data distribution; 3. an inverter was proposed to map the time series data back to latent space and the status indicator based on reconstruction error was developed for fault detection. A big normal training dataset was obtained using a Simulink version Tennessee Eastman process simulation and experimental results show that the proposed method can capture dynamic characteristics from big data set and reduces the false alarm rate compared with the traditional method, which verifies the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-ion Batteries Using an Improved Extreme Learning Machine Approach
abstract: Accurate state of charge (SOC) estimation is of great significance for a lithium-ion battery to ensure its safe operation and prevent it from over-charging or over-discharging. However, it is difficult to get an accurate value of SOC since it is an inner state of a battery cell, which cannot be directly measured. In order to improve the estimation accuracy of SOC, this paper develops a SOC estimation model for a lithium-ion battery using a Particle Swarm Optimization-Extreme Learning Machine(PSO-ELM) algorithm. The PSO is applied to determine the optimal value of hidden layer neurons and the learning rate since these parameters are the most critical factors in constructing an optimal ELM model. The inputs to the PSO-ELM model are the battery voltage, current, and temperature, and the output is the actual SOC values. The performance of the proposed model is compared with BP neural network and ELM models and verified based on the mean square error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and SOC error. The results demonstrate that the PSO-ELM model offers higher accuracy and lower SOC error rate than ELM and BP neural network models.

articleTitle: Rotation Speed Estimation for Motor Fault Diagnosis Using Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory Networks
abstract: Rotation speed estimation is a key step for motor fault diagnosis under variable-speed working conditions. This study investigates a method for speed estimation by fusing the information from vibration and current signals using a bidirectional long short term memory (BiLSTM) deep neural networks. Firstly, the instantaneous frequency (IF) curves are extracted from the signals using an improved time-frequency analysis method. A BiLSTM regression model is trained for IFs fusion and rotation speed estimation. Finally, the rotation angle is computed from the estimated rotation speed curve, and the vibration signal is resampled and processed for motor fault diagnosis. The performance of the proposed method is validated by the experimental data acquired from a switched reluctance motor test rig.

articleTitle: UAV Landing Control Disturbed by Carrier Air-Wake Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: A method based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed to solve the autonomous landing control problem of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) under the interference of carrier air-wake. Firstly, a simulation model of UAV landing on a carrier is built, and a reference trajectory to ensure its safe landing is designed. Secondly, a UAV autonomous landing control method based on Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm is proposed, and the reward function is designed that takes into account tracking error and trajectory stability. Finally, through offline training, an autonomous landing controller is obtained. The simulation results show that the controller designed in this paper can not only accurately control the landing trajectory of UAVs, but also cope with complex effects of nonlinear air-wake in nonlinear dynamic inverse (NDI) control, and greatly improve the safety of landing.

articleTitle: Estimation and Control of Networked Control Systems under Joint Attacks
abstract: For the design of attack-resilient controller, most of the existing results focus on preventing false data injection (FDI) attacks. Unlike the existing papers, this paper proposes a co-design control frame in presence of denial-of-service (DoS)attacks and FDI attacks. First, an observer with the ability to simultaneously estimate state vectors and FDI attack vectors is developed. Second, a controller is constructed using state estimates. In order to prevent the attack signal from entering the system and affecting the stability of the system, a switching system is proposed. The results show that the closed-loop system is stable with a prescribed ℋ<inf>∞</inf> performance and has the ability to resist attack. Finally, the validity of the controller and the correctness of the theory are verified by the simulation of the proposed numerical example.

articleTitle: UAV-USV cooperative tracking based on MPC
abstract: To address the problem of cooperative real-time tracking of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned surface vehicle (USV), a real-time tracking control strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed. Firstly, the mathematical models of UAV and USV are established, and then the trajectory generated by USV heave motion is taken as the constraint condition of MPC; furthermore, the UAV-USV cooperative tracking problem is transformed into a quadratic programming problem with constraints, and the Hildreth algorithm for solving the quadratic programming problem is improved to ensure the real-time performance of the UAV-USV tracking process. Simulation experiments show that the designed model predictive controller can realize the real-time trajectory tracking of UAV-USV. The improved Hildreth algorithm also has a higher operation speed, which effectively ensures the real-time tracking of UAV-USV.

articleTitle: Research on Public Cycle Allocation of Arterial Based on the Tail Vehicle Departure Model
abstract: The coordinated control of arterial signals generally selects the maximum cycle of isolated intersection timing as the common cycle to meet the traffic capacity requirements of each intersection in the artery. Aiming at the lack of research on how to allocate redundant cycles at non-critical intersections after the maximum cycle is selected, isolated intersection redundant cycle allocation method based on the tail vehicle departure model and the phase traffic volume interval is proposed. First, determine the traffic volume interval of each phase of the intersection according to the traffic volume of each phase of the intersection. The lower limit of the interval is the average traffic volume, and the upper limit of the interval is a value that can contain most of the traffic volume points. Then, according to the starting characteristics of vehicles, the model between the length of vehicle queue and the phase time required to be released is established and compared with the classical stop line method. Finally, the excess cycle is allocated according to the upper and lower limits of the traffic volume interval, and the allocation follows the principle of "providing a higher level of service for the coordinated phase on the basis of ensuring the capacity of the uncoordinated phase". The analysis shows that the method proposed in this paper has high practicability. It can not only meet the non-green wave phase capacity, but also has a better optimization effect on the green wave phase.

articleTitle: Active vibration suppression and attitude tracking for flexible spacecraft without intelligent materials
abstract: This paper investigates active vibration suppression and attitude tracking for flexible spacecraft under model uncertainty and external disturbance without flexible vibration measurement and intelligent materials. An adaptive control scheme based on a novel sliding mode surface is designed to suppress the flexible vibration introduced by flexible appendages and realize the attitude tracking. The remarkable feature of the designed algorithm is that flexible vibration is suppressed and attitude tracking is guaranteed simultaneously without intelligent materials and flexible vibration measurement. In addition, high precision attitude control can be achieved when flexible vibration is suppressed. The stability of the proposed control scheme is presented by Lyapunov techniques. Finally, simulation results are given to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Abnormal Data Detection and Cleaning of Wind Turbines Based on Average Confidence Interval Method
abstract: wind turbine SCADA (Supervisory control and data acquisition) data contains a considerable proportion reflecting abnormal operation. Accurately eliminating these abnormal data is the basis for subsequent wind turbine power prediction and generation performance evaluation. This paper proposes a method for cleaning abnormal operation data of wind turbines based on average confidence interval. First of all, all wind turbine operational data are allocated into different bins at a certain interval in the horizontal power direction, and the adaptive kernel density method is used to successively establish the probability density distribution of operation data in each horizontal power bin. Next, the distribution characteristics of abnormal data points are obtained by analyzing the shape of probability density curve. Finally, an average confidence interval method is used to eliminate abnormal data. With actual wind turbine SCADA data, the proposed method is proved to be effective.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency-based fixed-time control for nonlinear system
abstract: This paper investigates the energy efficiency problem of fixed-time control for nonlinear system where input energy, initial conditions and convergence time are considered. Note that, different from existing conventional fixed-time results, a concept of energy efficiency between actual input power, initial values and convergence time is introduced. Based on the energy efficiency concept, a proper trade-off is carried out, and a novel energy efficiency-based fixed-time control scheme for nonlinear system is constructed. By using fixed-time stable theory and appropriate Lyapunov function, fixed-time controllers are developed to ensure the desired performance can be achieved within allowed energy efficiency range and a preset fixed time. Finally, the stability analysis and simulation examples are both provided to verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive fuzzy fixed-time congestion control for TCP/AWM networks
abstract: This paper investigates the fixed-time congestion control problem for a class of TCP/AWM networks. Inspired by existing network models, a modified TCP/AWM network model with the variable number of TCP sessions and the external disturbance is first established. Moreover, fuzzy logic systems and bound estimation method are respectively introduced to deal with the nonlinear functions and the external disturbance in the system. At the same time, a new performance function, called fixed-time performance function, is first defined in this paper, where combining it with prescribed performance control guarantees that the desired queue length is tracked by the queue length in fixed-time. In addition, the proposed congestion control algorithm with the aid of backstepping technique can ensure that all the signals of the closed-loop system remain semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded. Finally, a set of simulation studies are provided to clarify the effectiveness and superiority of the designed congestion controller.

articleTitle: Path Tracking and Obstacle Avoidance Algorithm Based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: Path tracking and obstacle avoidance are key technologies in the field of intelligent driving. This paper is to solve path tracking and obstacle avoidance problems based on Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithm. Firstly, the vehicle kinematics model is established. Based on the vehicle model, the MPC algorithm is used to study the path tracking problem. Secondly, the nonlinear model MPC path tracking controller is designed, the simulation analysis and comparison are performed, where the obstacle avoidance problem is also considered, and MPC obstacle avoidance tracking controller is designed. Real-time experiments also validate the controller design.

articleTitle: Photosynthetic Rate Prediction Model of Greenhouse Crops Based on PLS-ELM
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low prediction accuracy caused by the large amount of calculation and artificially selected parameters when the traditional extreme learning machine (ELM) algorithm is used to establish the photosynthetic rate prediction model of greenhouse crops, a prediction model of photosynthetic rate based on extreme learning machine combining with partial least squares method (PLS-ELM) is established in this paper. Firstly, the sample data were obtained by measuring the photosynthetic rate under the combination of multiple environmental factors. Secondly, a photosynthetic rate modeling method based on PLS-ELM is proposed, that is, the number of hidden layer neurons and network weights of extreme learning machine algorithm are optimized by partial least squares (PLS), and the Softmax is selected as the activation function to improve the fitting accuracy of the model established by ELM algorithm. Finally, the experimental results show that the photosynthetic rate prediction model established by this method has high accuracy.

articleTitle: Image Stitching Based on Feature Optimization of Bayesian Probability Model
abstract: The goal of image stitching is to create a natural mosaic without ghosts, local distortions and artifacts. Towards this end, this paper presents a local feature optimization method based on Bayesian probability model for the image stitching. The spatially-varying algorithm is employed to perfectly align the entire overlapping area of images. A local feature optimization Bayesian probability model is then proposed to remove incorrect matching points in the images aiming to obtain a more accurate local homography estimation for robust alignment. Moreover, the strategy of combining local warping and similarity transformation is applied to reduce the distortion of non-overlapping regions. The salient features of the proposed method are that it is highly compatible with other image transformations and can effectively solve the inevitable ghosting problem of image stitching. Finally, experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Input-to-output stability of the nonlinear singular systems and small-gain theorem
abstract: This paper studies the input-to-output stability (IOS) of nonlinear singular systems and presents the output-Lagrange IOS (OL-IOS) small-gain theorem of the interconnected singular system. The major contribution of this paper includes three aspects. Firstly, the IOS property and OL-IOS property of nonlinear singular systems is established. Secondly, the conditions of IOS small-gain theorem for the interconnected singular system is obtained. Thirdly, the theorems for OL-IOS and the trajectory-based small-gain theorem of interconnected singular system are proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of proposed method is illustrated by using a numerical example.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Finite Time Hyperbolic Sine Tracking Differentiator
abstract: In the high precision photoelectric servo stabilized platform, the extraction of differential signals is essential. In allusion to the problem that the design parameters of tracking differentiator are difficult to be selected and sensitive to noise, a finite-time tracking differentiator is designed, which could input the arbitrary order derivative and effectively suppress the noise. Simulation results show that the finite-time hyperbolic sine tracking differentiator (FSTD) designed in this paper has advantages in the derivative estimation accuracy and noise suppression of input signals. It is applied to simulation platform and verified.

articleTitle: Direct Force Control of PMLSM Based on Fractional-order Model Reference Adaptive System
abstract: Given the traditional integer-order model reference adaptive system (IOMRAS) with large speed estimation error, slow response speed and poor performance against external interference under the direct force control (DFC) of permanent magnet linear synchronous motor (PMLSM), a fractional-order model reference adaptive system (FOMRAS) algorithm is proposed, which adopts the concept of fractional calculus and fractional-order Lyapunov stability theory. Through analysis and calculation, the fractional adaptive law is used to control the system in speed identification, which improves the speed tracking performance, reduces the oscillation of force response and ensures that the estimated value quickly approaches the real value. Then it is applied to DFC to realize speed sensorless control. The simulation results show that the speed sensorless PMLSM-DFC based on FOMRAS has significantly enhanced anti-disturbance performance and good dynamic and static performance, thus ensuring the stability of the system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fractional Order Sliding Mode Control for UAVs Formation with Actuator Faults
abstract: In this article, the distributed tracking control problem is studied for the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) formation with actuator faults and external disturbances. In order to make the UAVs formation have superior tracking performance during the mission, an adaptive fractional order sliding mode (FOSM) controller with great dynamic performance is proposed. The adverse effects of actuator faults and external disturbances are considered during the flight, and cerebellar model articulation neural networks (CMANN) are introduced to approximately compensate the effects of actuator faults and unknown disturbances. At the same time, it guarantees the global stability of the closed-loop system under the controller, and the simulation example verifies that the method has certain advantages in practical applications.

articleTitle: Sequential Fast Covariance Intersection Fusion Kalman Filter For Multi-Sensor Networked Systems with Correlated Noises and Random Uncertainties
abstract: For the multi-sensor systems with correlated noises and random uncertainties, a new augmented state approach with fictitious noises and a Sequential Fast Covariance Intersection (SFCI) fusion Kalman filter are presented. These algorithms can compensate the mixed random uncertainties with the fictitious noises, which include the random one-step measurements and missing measurements, and decrease the large computational burden. Furthermore, the SFCI fusion algorithm overcomes the drawback of the Sequential Covariance Intersection (SCI) fusion, whose fusion result is sensitive to the fusion orders, and improves the accuracy and efficiency. The accuracy of the presented SFCI fusion Kalman filter is higher than that of each local estimator, less but close to that of the information fusion Kalman estimator weighted by matrices. Finally, the effectiveness of the SFCI fusion Kalman algorithm is verified by the simulation example.

articleTitle: Collision detection framework based on Unity3D
abstract: With the development and application of Unity3D, more and more individual developers and small teams use it to develop their own products. However, in order to get the products as soon as possible, individual developers and small teams often ignore the problem of collision detection. In order to reduce the cost of collision detection technology for individual developers and small teams in simulation or game development, this paper proposes a universal collision detection framework. The main algorithms of the framework are AABB bounding box, SDF and GJK. In the aspect of logic processing, the framework distinguishes and processes the different collision situations between static objects and dynamic objects. Finally, the experimental results show that the frame rate can be effectively improved in a certain range.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Based on Fault Tree and Bayesian Network with Grey Optimization
abstract: Remote-controlled engine ignition of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is the key node for its successful flight mission. The effective fault diagnosis and prevention of remote-controlled engine is the guarantee of its safe and reliable operation. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on the fusion of fault tree (FT) and Bayesian network (BN). Further, a grey analysis model is employed to mine the in-depth information of the FT model, so as to find the key factors affecting the ignition failure of the remote-controlled engine, and provide support for maintenance and product design. Finally, the correctness and validity of the proposed model are verified by using a the typical fault mode of the remote-controlled engine.

articleTitle: Government Mechanisms in Closed-loop Supply Chain considering Retailer’s Dual-channel Structure
abstract: In order to analyze how different government mechanisms affect decisions in closed-loop supply chain with retailers' dual-channel structure, three game models were established. The result showed that when the government adopts the reward-penalty mechanism, too small reward-penalty parameter cannot achieve effective supervision and motivation; When the government adopts the processing fund mechanism, members’ profits decrease in the forward supply chain while increase in the reverse supply chain; The reward-penalty mechanism has no effect on the product’s price, but the processing fund mechanism will increase the product’s price. What’s more, the profit of members in the forward supply chain under reward-penalty mechanism is always better when compared with the processing fund mechanism. While in the reverse supply chain, the profit of members depends on the relative value of government's subsidy and reward-penalty parameter.

articleTitle: A single-layer neural network based robust adaptive control of a class of motor system with torque-control
abstract: Motor systems are widely used in various fields, and its high-precision control has always been a hot research topic. In this paper, the back propagation neural network (BPNN) is used to estimate the interference in the motor system. On this basis, a robust adaptive controller is designed for a type of motor system with torque control to achieve high precision Motion control. The BPNN based on the interference observer and the robust adaptive controller are integrated through the feedforward cancellation technology to achieve the high performance of the motor system. The nonlinear controller can theoretically achieve the final bounded stability, which can be proved by Lyapunov analysis. Therefore, the designed controller can handle the strong parameter uncertainty and strong external interference in the motor system. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Fabric Defect Image Segmentation Method Based on The Combination of Canny and Morphology
abstract: In order to filter out the background noise while retaining the characteristics of the defects, this paper combines Canny and morphological processing to segment the fabric defects. After image preprocessing, our improved algorithm is used to detect the defects, and considering the characteristics of the fabric image, when using the morphology closed operation, the cross-shaped kernel and the rectangular kernel are combined to separate the defect and the background. The defect area obtained by the improved algorithm is compared with the defect area obtained by the expert manual marking method. The defect area obtained by the improved algorithm has a proportion of more than 85%, which proves that our proposed algorithm is effective in the field of image segmentation.

articleTitle: Appointed-time tracking control for uncertain nonstrict-feedback nonlinear systems with output constraint
abstract: A novel appointed-time adaptive tracking control scheme is proposed for a class of uncertain nonstrict-feedback nonlinear systems with output constraint. First, a modified nonlinear state transformation is constructed to guarantee the output constraint. And desired tracking performance of the actual output can be obtained by directly manipulating the output tracking error of the transformed system. Then, a new shifting error transformation is introduced in the control design to ensure that the tracking error converges into a pregiven interval in appointed time even when the initial tracking condition is unknown. Backstepping technique, dynamic surface control method as well as fuzzy approximators are applied to formulated the adaptive controller, and the stability of the proposed control scheme is theoretically proved, and the effectiveness is numerically validated.

articleTitle: Serve control of galvo system based on improved extended state observer
abstract: In order to improve the robustness and tracking accuracy of the galvanometer (galvo) system, a sliding mode control strategy based on an improved extended state observer (ESO) is proposed. First, combining the sliding mode variable structure control theory, a new type of optimal control function is designed to replace the nonlinear function in the traditional ESO, and the structure of the traditional ESO is optimized. At the same time, fuzzy control is used to track and compensate the time-varying total disturbance in real time. This improves the observation accuracy of the observer and simplifies the parameter tuning process. Finally, through simulation and comparison, the proposed control scheme is verified. The results show that the control strategy effectively improves the tracking accuracy of thegalvo system and has better anti-interference ability. This is the paper style requirement for the Chinese Control and Decision Conference. The writers of papers should and must provide normalized electronic documents in order for readers to search and read papers conveniently.

articleTitle: Pursuit-Evasion Strategy of Multi-USV System in Complex Marine Environment with Time-Varying Ocean Current
abstract: To solve the target with speed advantage pursuit problem, this paper presents a kind of capture strategy for multiple unmanned surface vehicles to capture a target unmanned surface vehicle in a complex marine environment with time-varying current and unknown obstacles.
